author: alvoron
title: JS API E2E Electron cleanup fails with Permission Denied on Windows runner
signature: rm cannot remove electron.exe Permission denied|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: JS API (24)
failed_jobs.symptom: E2E Electron test teardown fails: rm cannot remove electron.exe/d3dcompiler_47.dll: Permission denied

key_errors:
exec error: Error: Command failed: rm -rf demo-electron-app-project
rm: cannot remove 'demo-electron-app-project/node_modules/electron/dist/d3dcompiler_47.dll': Permission denied
rm: cannot remove 'demo-electron-app-project/node_modules/electron/dist/electron.exe': Permission denied
rm: cannot remove 'demo-electron-app-project/node_modules/electron/dist/libGLESv2.dll': Permission denied
root_cause: The E2E Electron test's 'after all' cleanup hook attempts to delete the demo-electron-app-project directory via 'rm -rf'. On Windows runners, the Electron binary and DLLs (electron.exe, d3dcompiler_47.dll, libGLESv2.dll) remain locked by the OS after the Electron process completes, causing Permission Denied errors. This is a Windows-specific infrastructure/runner issue unrelated to the PR changes (which only touch GPU plugin deconvolution shape inference). The actual tests passed (2 passing); only the cleanup hook failed.
reproduction_steps: Run E2E Electron tests on a Windows CI runner where Electron binaries may remain locked after the test process exits.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed job — the lock is transient and typically releases between runs
Consider using 'rimraf' or PowerShell 'Remove-Item -Recurse -Force' instead of 'rm -rf' in the Electron E2E cleanup hook for Windows compatibility
Add retry logic or a delay before cleanup in the 'after all' hook
prevention_strategies: Use Windows-compatible cleanup commands in test teardown. Consider using rimraf npm package or PowerShell for directory removal on Windows runners.
historical_context: No prior occurrence of this exact signature found in the investigation database.
